subtitle: Peak / RMS Compressor with Saturator
tagline: Precise peak or RMS compression with lookahead, an external sidechain with filters, and an optional saturator with circuit-derived colour models.

body.lead: TB Compressor is a single-band compressor for tracks, buses, and full mixes. It reduces the level of loud passages above a threshold, and lets you shape how quickly it reacts, how smoothly it starts, and what it listens to.

body.p: Next to the classic controls you get a peak or RMS detector, lookahead, stereo linking, an external sidechain input with its own filters, and a saturator that adds harmonic colour after compression. Oversampling up to 8x keeps the saturator clean.

ul: Threshold, ratio, soft knee, attack, release, and makeup gain
Peak detection, or 50 ms RMS detection that follows the average level
Up to 20 ms lookahead so the compressor can react before a peak arrives
External sidechain with high-pass and low-pass filters on the detector
Stereo link, so both channels receive the same gain reduction
Saturator with six types (Clean, Soft, Hard, Punch, Warm, Tape) and five circuit-derived models
Transfer curve, six-second level history, and IN, OUT, and GR readouts

note.title: About this manual
text: This manual describes TB Compressor 2.1.0 for Windows (VST3). The current macOS build is version 1.1.3 and may differ from the descriptions here.

ol: Insert TB Compressor on a track or bus. The defaults are a gentle starting point: `THRESH` −18 dB, `RATIO` 2:1, `KNEE` 6 dB, `ATTACK` 10 ms, `RELEASE` 100 ms.
Play the loudest part and lower `THRESH` until the GR readout {{3}} shows the amount of reduction you want, typically 2 to 6 dB.
Set `ATTACK`: longer times let the start of each note through for more punch; shorter times catch peaks.
Set `RELEASE` so the gain recovers in time with the music, without audible pumping.
Raise `MAKEUP` {{8}} until the compressed signal matches the bypassed level, then compare with bypass.
Optional: switch on the `SATURATOR` {{11}} and raise `DRIVE` for colour, or connect an external sidechain {{10}} for ducking.

rows: Compression threshold. Signals above it are reduced; the lower it is, the more of the program is compressed.
Compression ratio: how strongly level above the threshold is reduced. High ratios limit transients firmly.
Knee width. A wide knee starts compressing gently just below the threshold; 0 dB gives a hard knee.
How quickly gain reduction reaches its target. Too fast dulls the attack of notes; too slow lets the first peak through.
How quickly the gain recovers. Short times can pump; long times can keep the next note down.
Peak reacts to instantaneous peaks. RMS follows a 50 ms average and controls sustained energy rather than short peaks.
Input trim before the detector and delay line. It changes how hard the compressor is driven.
Gain added after compression to restore level.
Lookahead: lets the detector react before a peak reaches the output. It adds latency.
Runs the processing at a higher sample rate to reduce aliasing from saturation. Higher settings use more CPU and add latency.
Links gain reduction across channels so the stereo image stays steady. Off lets each channel compress on its own.

warn.text: TB Compressor uses a delay line of up to 20 ms for lookahead, and oversampling adds further latency. It is designed for mixing rather than zero-latency monitoring while recording.

body.p: By default the detector listens to the audio being compressed (INT). When your DAW sends a signal to TB Compressor's sidechain input, the indicator changes to EXT and the detector listens to that key signal instead, for example a kick drum that ducks a bass or a voice that ducks music. The external key is used only when the sidechain bus is active in your DAW.

rows: High-pass filter on the external key (host name Sidechain Low Cut). Removes low frequencies from what the detector hears.
Low-pass filter on the external key (host name Sidechain High Cut). Removes high frequencies from what the detector hears.

note.text: The sidechain filters shape only what the detector hears. They do not filter the audio you hear, and they work only with an external key (FILTERS ON WITH EXT SC).

body.p: The saturator sits after compression and adds harmonic colour. Switch it on with `ON`, set the amount with `DRIVE`, and blend it with `MIX`. The circuit model selects the character: Legacy, or the circuit-derived VCA, opto, FET, and vari-mu colour models XXL, LX-2X, FET-X76, and FX-67X. The type selector sets the Legacy saturation type.

rows: Saturation drive. Higher values add more harmonics and density.
Legacy, XXL, LX-2X, FET-X76, FX-67X · Legacy
Clean, Soft, Hard, Punch, Warm, Tape · Clean

tip.text: Compare the saturator at matched loudness. Saturation adds harmonics and level, which can make it seem better than it is.

body.p: Step through presets with the arrows in the preset browser {{1}}. LOAD FROM FILE opens a saved .tbcpreset file, and Save stores the current state as a file. Undo and Redo step through recent changes.
Factory presets: **Clean Control**, **Vocal Leveler**, **Drum Punch**, **Bus Glue**, and **Sidechain Duck**.
Starting points for common jobs. Adjust them by ear and check the GR readout.

recipes.title: Level a vocal
recipes.use: Even out a vocal performance without squashing it.
steps: Lower THRESH until only the loud phrases are reduced.

recipes.title: Add punch to drums
recipes.use: More impact from kick, snare, or a drum bus.
steps: Lengthen ATTACK until the hit's initial crack comes through.
Shorten RELEASE until the gain recovers before the next hit.

recipes.title: Glue a mix bus
recipes.use: Make a mix feel more cohesive.
steps: Keep reduction small; the bus should breathe, not pump.

recipes.title: Duck bass with the kick
recipes.use: Make room for the kick by ducking the bass on each hit.
settings: Around 150 Hz to focus on the kick
steps: Route the kick to TB Compressor's sidechain input in your DAW.
Lower THRESH until the bass dips on each kick.

rows: The track sounds better only because it is louder.
Match levels with MAKEUP or OUTPUT and compare with bypass at the same loudness.
Lengthen ATTACK, lower RATIO, or try the PEAK detector with less reduction.
Lengthen RELEASE or reduce the amount of gain reduction.
The stereo image shifts while compressing.
Check that your DAW routes a signal to the sidechain input and that the indicator shows EXT.
They affect only an external key, and only what the detector hears.
Lookahead and oversampling add latency. Set LOOKAHD to 0 ms and oversampling to 1x for the lowest delay.
